output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification and distinctions (site comparison), then ACH across hypotheses, with a provenance check on the sources.
output.brief:
Cancelling RotaWeave would probably not fix this. The drop is concentrated at Dock Street and Westgate, which lost their coordinator on 1 May and also use the app. Millbrook has the app but kept its coordinator, and it is nearly flat (118 to 111). Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but is not on the app, and it is also nearly flat (86 to 80). So neither change alone explains the fall. Together they do.

The app's basic tier has no recurring bookings. A regular keeps a weekly slot only if staff book it before Thursday's release. Staff bookings at Dock Street and Westgate fell from 74 a week to 3 after the coordinator left, and one admin seat sits unused. Of 213 April regulars at those two sites, 129 lost their usual slot at least twice, and 88% of those are now inactive. Among the 61 volunteers reached by phone, 44 said nobody booked them.

The background check is not the cause. 21 of the 23 people deactivated were reactivated, and 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current check. Commonplate looks minor: only 2 of the 61 callbacks joined another group.

Next steps: assign someone to book regulars into their usual slots at Dock Street and Westgate before each Thursday release, and phone lapsed regulars to offer their slot back. Keep the background check, keep the contract for now, and do not remove inactive people from the roster or the retention figures. Confidence is fairly high. The main gap is that the callback sample is small.
